title: The Names of the Word
english: The deep and great mystery is immediately spoken of, and it is in need of guidance from above. For it was revealed to the blessed Peter. The Word is God, co-eternal and co-throned with God the Father, co-existing and co-eternal. The names held naturally to his nature before the incarnation are God, wisdom, light, life, and power. Other names are found among the sacred writings.

Since he emptied himself by becoming in the likeness of a man, and was found in the form of a man, he receives the common name, that is, Christ and Jesus, or rather, Emmanuel. The name Emmanuel signifies 'God with us.' For it is written, 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel' (Isaiah 7:14). For the blessed Gabriel revealed the mystery to the holy and God-bearing virgin, saying, 'Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor with God, and behold, you shall conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus. For he shall save his people from their sins' (Matthew 1:21-23). Are the prophet and the blessed angel inconsistent with one another? Not at all. For the blessed prophet speaks mysteries by the Spirit, having foretold a God who has become with us, naming him so both from his nature and from the economy of the flesh. But the blessed angel gave him the name through his own activity, for he said, 'He shall save his own people.' Thus, he is called Savior because of this.

Indeed, when the armies of the angels were evangelizing the birth to the shepherds, saying, 'Do not fear, for behold, we are evangelizing to you today a great joy, which is for all the people, that a Savior was born today, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David' (Luke 2:10-11), he endured the birth according to the flesh for our sake. Therefore, Emmanuel, because being God by nature he became with us, that is, a human being. And Jesus, because he had to save those under heaven, being God and having become a man. When he came forth from the womb of his own mother—for that which is according to the flesh was born from her—then his name was called. It is not fitting, I say, for the name of Christ to be applied to the Word of God before the birth according to the flesh. For he was not yet anointed, how could he be called Christ? When he came forth from the womb of a mother as a man, then he receives the calling in conjunction with the birth according to the flesh.

It is said that his mouth is like a sharp two-edged sword. This is also true. For it is written somewhere about him, or rather the prophet Isaiah himself says: 'And he will be girded with righteousness around his waist, and truth will have taken hold of his...'
translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence: '...λεν ἐν τούτοις...'
The translation of 'εὐαγγελιζόμεθα' as 'we are evangelizing' is based on the present tense of the verb, indicating an ongoing action.
The translation of 'ἐτέχθη' as 'was born' is based on the aorist tense of the verb, indicating a completed action.

title: Divine Salvation
english: The measure of emptiness has been poured out upon us, and it is proclaimed to the chosen ones that in an acceptable time, God listened to them and helped them on a day of salvation.
This proclamation is rooted in the fact that Christ was foreknown before the foundation of the world, and his mystery was also foreknown.
He appeared at the times which the Ruler wished, and at those times, he was made known to us, with the time of his becoming human being a day of salvation.
The divine Paul also affirms this, saying, 'Behold, now is the acceptable time, behold, now is the day of salvation' (2 Corinthians 6:2).
Similarly, the prophet David expresses his joy, saying, 'This is the day which the Lord made, let us rejoice and be glad in it' (Psalm 118:24).
As the Lord says, 'In an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you' (Isaiah 49:8), these words are spoken by God and the Father to our Savior Christ.
The Lord gave a covenant to the nations, to establish the earth and to inherit a deserted inheritance, saying to those in bonds, 'Come out,' and to those in darkness, 'Be revealed' (Isaiah 49:9).

He will feed them on all their ways, and they will not hunger, nor will they thirst, nor will the heat strike them, nor the sun, but the one who has mercy on them will comfort them, and he will lead them through springs of water, and every mountain will be made a way, and every path a pasture for them.
Behold, these are coming from afar, and these are from the north, and these are from the sea, and others are from the land of the Persians.

Some preceding interpreters considered this passage to be the beginning of the present chapter, which starts with the words, 'In an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you'.
Before the precious cross, Christ prayed, saying, 'Father, if possible, let this cup pass from me' (Matthew 26:39), but he was not heard, for he had willed it.
Since he had willed death, being taken over by the Father, it was said to him necessarily, 'In an acceptable time I heard you, and on a day of salvation I helped you'.

It seems to me that the word is very trustworthy, for although Christ knew he had to drink the cup and that salvation would not be possible unless through his death and resurrection, the shape of his prayer was done economically, so that the avoidance of passion would accuse the Jews' impiety.

For in what way did Israel become guilty of the sins of impiety against him, if it was not unwilling for him to suffer; however, it became willing, and the sin of the world was taken away, and our things were remade into newness of holy life, as he said, 'I came down from heaven, not to do my will, but the will'.
Understanding this, we see that Christ's prayer was part of a larger plan.
The Greek source ends mid-word at 'the will', so the final quotation is rendered literally as an incomplete thought.
translator_notes: The Greek source ends mid-word at 'τὸ θέλημ' ('the will'), so the final quotation is rendered literally as an incomplete thought.

title: The Church's Growth Through Faith
english: The multitude of those who will be called is indeed large and countless, indicating the vast number of people who will be part of the Church.
The sons who were lost will say to their mother, 'Make room for me,' as they return to her.

This is also said to the intelligible Zion, which is the Church, 'Enlarge the place of your tent and stretch out the curtains of your dwellings. Do not spare, but extend to the right and to the left' (Isaiah 54:2).

We read in the books of Moses that the tent in the wilderness had wide and spacious curtains, which were made through the hands of the skilled workers, some facing east and the rising sun, others behind the tent to the west, and also to the north and south, indicating the future breadth and length of the holy courts, or the churches.

However, even though the grace from Christ is always abundant, the places are narrow for those who believe, so that the Church, which is the intelligible Zion, rejoices and says to itself, 'Who has borne these for me?'
I would say that it is faith in Christ, through which the Church, though once childless and a widow, has become numerous in children.
Faith has nourished the people, and the Church, once seized and alone, has been unexpectedly clothed and has appeared with many children, who were once naked and alone.

Thus says the Lord, 'Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my signal to the islands, and they will bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters on their shoulders. And kings will be your nurses, and queens your wet nurses; they will bow down to you and lick the dust of your feet' (Isaiah 49:22-23).
You will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be ashamed or embarrassed.

Having promised to Zion that she will be many-childed and fertile, and that her children will come to her, so that she will need wider places and will be urged to expand her tent, it is true that the multitude of promised children to her is not from Israel, but from the multitude of the nations, and through them, the things are seen.
When Christ was made known to the nations through the evangelical preachings, he became high and renowned through the wonders he worked, and through the resurrection.
The hand indeed signifies the strength, that is the power, when the Lord says 'I will lift up my hand' it means to lift up and exalt.
The power of the apostolic and evangelical preachings has brought to him the ones from all over the world through faith in Christ.
The remnant of Israel will be saved, but this is a small and limited number.
baehrens: PG 70 In Is. book4-logos4 rem close
translator_notes: The phrase 'intelligible Zion' refers to the Church as a spiritual entity, rather than a physical location.
The text appears to be a commentary on biblical passages, including Isaiah 54:2 and 49:22-23.
